about.title: Tulare Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Tulare's economy runs on agriculture, packing houses, distribution centers, and the trucking that moves along Rt 137, Blackstone, Bardsley, and SR-99. Workers in these fields face real risks from heavy equipment, repetitive strain, forklifts, and vehicle traffic near job sites. In California, a workplace injury usually goes through workers' compensation regardless of who caused it, but that system doesn't cover everything a person loses, and it doesn't apply if someone outside your employer — a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver — contributed to your injury. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we simply help injured Tulare workers get in front of an independent attorney who can sort out whether a workers' comp claim, a third-party claim, or both apply to a specific situation. There's no cost to ask, and no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Tulare Workers Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Understanding the 30-Day Reporting Window
items.desc: California requires injured employees to notify their employer within 30 days to preserve workers' comp benefits. An attorney can help make sure that step, and everything after it, is handled correctly.

items.title: Spotting Third-Party Claims Workers' Comp Won't Cover
items.desc: If a subcontractor, equipment maker, or another driver contributed to a Tulare workplace injury, a separate claim outside the workers' comp system may be possible — but it carries its own 2-year deadline.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: California law makes it illegal for an employer to retaliate against a worker for reporting an injury or filing a claim. An independent attorney can advise on protecting your job while your claim moves forward.

items.question: Can I still see an attorney if I'm already getting workers' comp benefits?
items.answer: Yes. Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but if a third party — like an equipment manufacturer or another driver near SR-99 or Bardsley — contributed to your injury, a separate claim may still be worth exploring. An attorney can look at both angles at once.

items.question: What if my injury happened while driving for work near Blackstone or Rt 137?
items.answer: Work-related driving injuries can sometimes involve both a workers' comp claim and a third-party injury claim if another driver was at fault. Given Tulare's traffic patterns, especially around Friday afternoon peaks, this comes up more than people expect. An attorney can sort out which paths apply to your case.

items.question: Is there really no cost to talk to someone through LawProactive?
items.answer: Correct — LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, and attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery. There's no obligation to move forward after speaking with someone.
